How to Use This App
1. Logging a pitch — 3 taps every time

Once a game is started, every pitch works the same way, in this order:

  1. Pick the pitch type — Fastball, Changeup, whatever was actually thrown.
  2. Tap the zone grid twice. First tap = where it was called (where it was supposed to go). Second tap = where it actually went. Tap the exact same square both times if it hit the spot — it turns green.
  3. Tap what happened — Ball, Strike, In Play, or HBP. If it's In Play, one more tap for Pop Fly, Line Drive, or Ground Ball.

The app counts balls and strikes for you — 4 balls is a walk, 3 strikes is a strikeout, and either one automatically moves you to the next batter. No need to track the count yourself.

2. The tracking screen at a glance
  • Count (top left) — the ball-strike count for the batter up right now.
  • Batter indicator (top right, "Batter N of M") — tap it any time to give this batter a jersey number.
  • Undo Location — mid-tap and tapped the wrong zone? This backs up one tap at a time.
  • Undo Last — already logged the pitch but it was wrong? This removes the last pitch and puts the batter/count back to where they were.
  • Log strip — your last several pitches, newest first. Green = on target, red = missed.
  • Batters / Stats (top right) — jump to the batter-by-batter view or the game recap without losing your place.
3. Coming up to bat again

Once the lineup cycles back around to a batter, a banner appears above the pitch grid showing what happened last time they were up — including which pitch got the call. Handy for deciding what to throw this time.

4. Batter Breakdown

Tap Batters any time to see every batter's plate appearances, pitch by pitch.

  • The batter currently up is highlighted green; whoever batted right before them is yellow.
  • Tap a batter's name (with the ✎) to give them a jersey number.
  • For any ball put in play, tap the direction it went and whether it was an out or safe — this feeds straight into the recap.
5. Editing pitchers

Use Change pitcher any time from the tracking screen.

If you've tracked a pitcher before — this game or a past one — they'll show up as a chip under Previously used pitchers. Tap the chip to instantly fill in their name, number, and pitch types.

6. Stats / Game Recap

Tap Stats to see the full breakdown for the game so far.

  • Per-pitcher stats: on-target %, most-thrown pitch, and accuracy by pitch type.
  • By Batter table — tap any batter's name to jump straight to their card on the Batter Breakdown screen.
  • From here you can export a CSV, download the heatmap image, email a recap to a coach, or tap Back to game to keep tracking right where you left off.
Finalize Game locks the game for good once you're really done — no more pitches can be added, and there's no "un-finalize." If you need to change something after finalizing, delete the game from Game History and re-enter it from scratch.
7. Game History

Every game saves automatically as you track it — nothing to do on your end. Tap View Past Games from the home screen any time to resume, review, or delete a game.

💡 Tip: swipe right from the very left edge of the screen to go back a step, just like your phone's usual back gesture.
